title: Chiyya of Hagra
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Yevamot 116a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.116a.3-5): a bill of divorce was found in Sura in which was written, “In the town of Sura, I, Anan bar Chiyya…” The Rabbis searched from Sura to Nehardea, and there was no other Anan bar Chiyya except Anan bar Chiyya of Hagra. Hyman infers that his son Anan lived in the time of Abaye and Rava. Yuchasin wrote that he lived in Shmuel’s days; possibly its proof is from [Ketubot 21a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.21a.11), the document that came out of Mar Shmuel’s court in which was written “when Rav Anan bar Chiyya came,” and Yuchasin perhaps thought that he was the son of Chiyya of Hagra. Hyman distinguishes the two, for the witness before Shmuel was a Torah scholar, while Anan of Hagra lived later and the passage gives no proof that he was a Torah scholar.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Yevamot names Anan bar Chiyya of Hagra in the investigation of the divorce document. Ketubot describes Rav Anan bar Chiyya testifying before Shmuel’s court.

[Heilprin’s Anan notice](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2906&lang=en) puts the two reports together. So does [Hyman’s separate Anan entry](https://www.girsology.com/toledot.html?entry=h-d13eaa21b76f47f9&lang=en), where he argues that the later debate does not date the incident. Here Hyman argues that the two men were distinct.
